replies.author: @GalenWright74
replies.text: Actually, the north east corridor is the first high speed rail operation in THE US.  Amtrak has been running electrified metroliner trains between Boston and DC, via NYC since the 70s with normal high speeds of 120mph.  This predated the Acela service by decades.   In fact, the Pennsylvania Railroad laid the ground work for this a century ago.  Yes, the north east corridor is aging, and is government run.  This has caused a lag in development and expansion.  But, this was the first for high speed rail in the country.

replies.author: @Batmans_Pet_Goldfish
replies.text:
The Acela was started by Amtrak in 2000 and the next gen one has only just started.

Granted, it only reaches highspeed on certain sections, as it also shares a lot of its route with the already existing rail infrastructure.

That said, if you want to find a true highspeed rail, Florida has the Brightline. It's privately owned, so ticket prices aren't exactly cheap, but there also not exactly terrible either. It goes between Miami and Orlando. Not huge, about half as long as Acela's route, and it travels slower, at most 120 mph, but the vast majority of its rail is traveling at those top speeds of about 110mph in the slower sections, so it's probably the closest thing we have to "true" highspeed rail.
